title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: mixtures of refractory metal elements (e.g., Nb, Mo, Ta, W, V)
recollection.intervention: Guess: thermodynamic/entropy-guided computational design followed by arc-melting synthesis
recollection.structure: Guess: single-phase body-centered cubic refractory high-entropy alloy
recollection.mechanism: Guess: high mixing entropy stabilizes BCC solid solution and suppresses intermetallic formation; valence electron concentration and atomic size mismatch used as design parameters
recollection.results: Guess: designed alloy exhibits yield strength >1.5 GPa at room temperature and retains >900 MPa at 1200 °C with reasonable ductility

score.note: The recollection generically identifies computational composition design followed by arc melting but misses the modulus/VEC screening, 38,326 compositions, and selected composition. Single-phase BCC is specifically correct. The proposed entropy/intermetallic mechanism does not match the paper’s VEC–Peierls barrier–dislocation mobility mechanism. The stated strengths and high-temperature performance are incorrect; the actual yield strength was about 1.12 GPa, with 35.7% compressive fracture strain and 2.55 GPa compressive strength.
